clue.text: Business charge including fellow's drink

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the charge holds the fellow's letter within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A firm's invoice adds a colleague's drinks to the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot beverage brewed from roasted beans is a drink, a straightforward example.

clue.text: Amorous glances from nasty fellow changing direction before seduction begins

indicators.note: a direction swaps here: right (R) is switched to left (L) in the nasty fellow

parts.note: an ogre is a cruel, monstrous person

indicators.note: begins asks for the opening letter of seduction

explanation.surface: A lecherous brute's sidelong looks lead to his attempt at seduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing direction' turns R (right) into L (left) inside OGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering, flirtatious looks are what the plural verb-noun means here: amorous glances.

clue.text: As one not paying for union privileges, I referred in error

definitions.text: one not paying for union privileges

indicators.note: something done in error is done wrongly, so these letters are set down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A worker admits they wrongly pointed someone towards union benefits without paying dues.
explanation.definitionFit: In labour relations, a person who enjoys union-won benefits without paying membership dues is the classic example of this term.

clue.text: Raise in relief exploded bombs, not one British, in European square

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the European and square letters

parts.note: S stands for square, as in sq and in measurements such as S for square in some tables

indicators.note: exploded bombs are blown apart, so the remaining letters are scattered
not one asks for just one of the two Bs to be dropped

explanation.surface: A war-torn European plaza where blown-up bombs once lay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' matters: the fodder has two of the British letter and only one goes, before 'exploded' scrambles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to carve or mould a design so it stands out raised from the surface, which is relief work.

clue.text: Soldier left undisciplined in apparent change of position

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
lax means slack, undisciplined

explanation.surface: A sloppy paratrooper wanders out of line during drill.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the shift an object seems to make against its background when the observer moves, a technical synonym.

clue.text: Son's a proper help — sadly one will have counsel in store

definitions.text: one will have counsel in store

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters come out badly arranged

explanation.surface: A parent laments that their boy is not much use, and someone will counsel him.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's paid assistant guides customers on what to buy, so they offer advice in a shop.

clue.text: Cavalier man's on a roll

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: A dashing fellow is enjoying a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' looks like an adjective meaning offhand; here it is a supporter of Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers were the king's supporters in the English Civil War, so a Cavalier is a monarchist.

clue.text: Centre of dish displays variety of 1

indicators.note: centre of asks for the dish word without its outer letters

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: The middle of a plate is given over to a display of the drink from 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso drink is one of the many ways the drink at 1 across is served.

clue.text: Nice aroma drifting about in kind of 1

indicators.note: letters drifting about move loosely out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant smell wafts around a coffee drink.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' refers to 1 across, COFFEE; 'Nice' looks like the French city but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso diluted with hot water is a style of the drink at 1 across.

clue.text: In Spain the brewed beer runs dry hence a type of wine is produced

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: brewed means concocted, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: In Spain the beer runs out, so people make wine instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Country wine is made from the dark fruit of the elder bush, so the fruit names a homemade wine.

clue.text: River supports

definitions.meaning: golf pegs that hold the ball up before a drive

explanation.surface: A river props things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A river in north-east England, and the small pegs golfers use to hold up the ball.

clue.text: Letter shape in convoluted prose is a kind of 1

indicators.note: the S-shape sits inside the rearranged prose
convoluted means twisted, so the letters of prose are twisted round

parts.note: an ess is the letter S, or something shaped like it

explanation.surface: A writer's tangled prose contains a coffee drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter shape' is the spelt-out name of the letter S, used for anything S-shaped; 'convoluted' scrambles prose around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong coffee forced through ground beans under pressure is a style of the drink at 1 across.

clue.text: Stays abed at home after first signs of severe enteric illness likely to return

indicators.note: after places the letters for at home behind the others
to return means the picked letters come back in reverse order
first signs of takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone stays home with a stomach bug that may recur.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying late in bed in the morning is staying abed, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Among a million one died

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Only one person in a million died.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means in the middle of, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Scot has talk about one over sort of 1

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman

indicators.note: about means the talk word goes round the one

parts.note: chat means talk
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A Scotsman chats about a coffee he has ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso marked with a dash of foamed milk is a style of the drink at 1 across.

clue.text: Animal lacking height has a tail wagging by end of run

indicators.note: a wagging tail moves to and fro, so the letters are shaken up
lacking means the word has loses a letter
end of takes the last letter of run

explanation.surface: A dog with a wagging tail runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' sits beside 'lacking height' as if describing a short dog, but 'lacking' acts on 'has', and 'wagging' then stirs the remains with 'a tail'.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd dog is a particular breed, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Strangely the laconic will have nothing to lose in kind of hitch

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters are arranged in an odd way
to lose means the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person will find nothing to say about a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' takes O from THE LACONIC, and 'Strangely' scrambles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical hitch is a mechanical or equipment fault, so the adjective qualifies a type of hitch.

clue.text: Cold follows hot in aortic malfunctioning of the chest

indicators.note: follows puts the cold letter behind the scrambled letters
malfunctioning means working wrongly, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A patient runs hot then cold when their aorta fails.
explanation.walkthrough: H and C are the hot and cold tap markings; 'malfunctioning' scrambles the hot letter with 'aortic'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the medical word for anything relating to the thorax, so it means of the chest.

clue.text: Covered in scratches, champion advances rapidly

indicators.note: covered in means the scratches word wraps round the champion

parts.note: scores are scratches or cut marks

explanation.surface: A battered winner pushes ahead quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratches' looks like a verb but is the noun SCORES.
explanation.definitionFit: To race at great speed, as a car does along a road, is an informal sense meaning to move fast.

clue.text: Make lovey-dovey noises to the Northern bird

parts.note: to coo is to murmur fondly, as doves do
t' is the northern English dialect shortening of the

explanation.surface: A northerner whispers sweet nothings to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern English dialect 'the' is clipped to t', as in 'down t' pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald-fronted water bird is a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: There's no right for rubbish around top of field to be spread

indicators.note: around means the trimmed rubbish word goes round the picked letter
no means the right letter is absent from the rubbish word

parts.note: refuse is rubbish

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of field

explanation.surface: Without a right to dump waste, rubbish gets scattered round a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no right' removes R from REFUSE, leaving EFUSE, which goes 'around' F.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to pour out or diffuse, so it is a synonym of spread in a liquid sense.

clue.text: Poet's beginning to recite most of song before the Queen

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the Queen
beginning to asks for the first letter of recite
most of drops the final letter of the song word

parts.note: a hymn is a religious song
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A poet starts by reciting part of a song in front of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester or versifier writes verse, so the word is a synonym, often slightly dismissive, for a poet.

clue.text: Instant tea variety of 1

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Instant tea passed off as one of the coffees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like a kind of drink but is a moment; '1' refers to 1 across, COFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The chocolate-flavoured drink is a style of the drink at 1 across.

clue.text: Occasional gesture's vulgar on looking back

indicators.note: looking back means the assembled pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a nod is a gesture of the head
naff is British slang for tasteless or vulgar
o is a clipped form standing for on

explanation.surface: A rude hand signal is made again now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' reverses NODNAFFO. NAFF is British slang for cheap and tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done intermittently, now and then, is occasional, an idiom synonym.

clue.text: Cat on one occasion grabbed emu's tail

indicators.note: grabbed means the occasion word holds the tail letter inside it

parts.note: once means on one occasion

indicators.note: tail picks the last letter of emu

explanation.surface: A big cat once caught an emu by the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called by this name, so it is a member of the cat family.

clue.text: Constituent of vital chemical that is found at the bottom of Moh's scale

definitions.text: that is found at the bottom of Moh's scale

indicators.note: constituent of means the letters form part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A vital chemical sits at the bottom of the mineral hardness scale.
explanation.walkthrough: Mohs scale ranks minerals by hardness from 1 to 10.
explanation.definitionFit: The softest mineral ranks 1 on the Mohs hardness scale, so it sits at the bottom.

clue.text: Top composer's ego lost over type of 1

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: lost means the ego letter goes missing from the composer

parts.note: Puccini was the Italian opera composer
I is the self, the ego
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A leading composer loses his self-importance over a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso topped with frothed milk is a style of the drink at 1 across.

clue.text: Cameron manoeuvres to right. He tries to woo us

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moves around, so the letters of the name are moved about

explanation.surface: Cameron shifts his party rightwards to court voters.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron was the UK Conservative Prime Minister when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor or wooer engages in romance, so the one who courts is the romantic pursuer.

clue.text: Net forms part of creels etc

indicators.note: forms part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A net is one item of a fisherman's kit along with baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Net forms' as the definition, but 'forms part of' is the whole hidden-word signal and the answer is a single net.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a net set in water to trap eels, so it is a specific kind of net.
